claim: The TβL genetic construct fuses a membrane segment to two antibiotic selection markers: β-lactamase and ToxR, which report on insertion and self-association, respectively.
source: The TβL genetic construct fuses a membrane segment to two antibiotic selection markers: β-lactamase and ToxR, which report on insertion and self-association, respectively.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1a showing the construct design.

claim: Bacterial survival on ampicillin monitors membrane integration.
source: In this construct, bacterial survival on ampicillin monitors membrane integration (Broome-Smith et al., 1990; Jaurin et al., 1982)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work establishing this relationship.

claim: Survival on chloramphenicol correlates with self-association of the membrane span.
source: survival on chloramphenicol correlates with self-association of the membrane span (Lis and Blumenthal, 2006; Russ and Engelman, 1999; Langosch et al., 1996)
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: β-lactamase and ToxR function only in the periplasm and cytoplasm, respectively.
source: Furthermore, β-lactamase and ToxR function only in the periplasm and cytoplasm, respectively
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the functional compartmentalization of these proteins.

claim: Only proteins inserted with their carboxy terminus located in the periplasm would be selected in the TβL assay.
source: therefore, unlike previous assays of membrane-protein insertion (Hessa et al., 2007), the orientation of the inserted segment relative to the membrane is known, and only proteins inserted with their carboxy terminus located in the periplasm would be selected
evidence: This is inferred from the functional requirements of β-lactamase and ToxR in specific cellular compartments.

claim: Survival on ampicillin depends linearly on β-lactamase expression levels.
source: Unlike this conventional TOXCAT experiment, in TβL survival on ampicillin depends linearly on β−lactamase expression levels (Broome-Smith et al., 1990; Jaurin et al., 1982; Li et al., 2004; Lis and Blumenthal, 2006)
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: TβL provides a more sensitive reporter for membrane insertion than MBP.
source: thus providing a more sensitive reporter for membrane insertion than MBP
evidence: This is inferred from the linear dependence of ampicillin survival on β-lactamase expression levels.

claim: The C-terminal portion of human L-Selectin (CLS) does not self-associate.
source: To minimize the effects of self-association on experimental readout, we chose the C-terminal portion of human L-Selectin (CLS), which does not self-associate (Srinivasan et al., 2011) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation and experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nine of the 10 selected single-point substitutions (all but Val302Lys) showed qualitatively similar trends of viability in deep sequencing and single-clone analysis.
source: Nine of the 10 selected single-point substitutions (all but Val302Lys) showed qualitatively similar trends of viability in deep sequencing and single-clone analysis.
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data from two different methods.

claim: The resolution of the deep-sequencing data is much greater than that seen in the single-clone assays.
source: The resolution of the deep-sequencing data, however, is much greater than that seen in the single-clone assays
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing specific ΔΔG values from the two methods.

claim: All tested clones expressed in the membrane fraction and ran at the expected size of ~55 kDa.
source: All clones expressed in the membrane fraction and ran at the expected size of ~55 kDa.
evidence: This is based on Western blot analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Six of the 10 tested mutations showed the expected trends in membrane localization.
source: Of the 10 tested mutations, 6 showed the expected trends, including mutations that increased (Met303Leu, Val304Phe, and Ala311Leu) or decreased expression (Val302Lys, Leu310Ala, and Ala311Arg) in agreement with the deep-sequencing and single-clone viability data
evidence: This is based on Western blot data comparing membrane localization with deep-sequencing results.

claim: Three mutants to charges at the amino terminus (Val311His, Met303Glu, and Val304Asp) increased expression levels according to Western blots but were disruptive according to dsTβL.
source: However, three mutants to charges at the amino terminus (Val311His, Met303Glu, and Val304Asp) increased expression levels according to Western blots but were disruptive according to dsTβL.
evidence: This is based on comparison of Western blot and dsTβL data.

claim: Ampicillin viability reports not only on membrane-expression levels but also on the appropriate membrane integration.
source: We attribute this difference to the fact that ampicillin viability reports not only on membrane-expression levels but also on the appropriate membrane integration, which is not captured by Western blots.
evidence: This is inferred from the discrepancy between Western blot and dsTβL results for certain mutants.

claim: The small and polar amino acids, Ser, Thr, and Cys have shallow, nearly neutral insertion profiles, ranging from −0.1 to +0.8 kcal/mol.
source: The small and polar amino acids, Ser, Thr, and Cys have shallow, nearly neutral profiles, ranging from −0.1 to +0.8 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The high disruptive profile of Gly and Pro emphasizes the strong unfavorable impact of exposing the polar protein backbone to the membrane environment.
source: emphasizing the strong unfavorable impact of exposing the polar protein backbone to the membrane environment
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed high energy penalty for Gly and Pro insertion.

claim: The large polar (Asn, His, and Gln) and charged residues (Asp, Glu, Lys, and Arg) are all highly disruptive in the membrane mid-plane.
source: The large polar (Asn, His, and Gln) and charged residues (Asp, Glu, Lys, and Arg) are all highly disruptive in the membrane mid-plane.
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The energetic penalties for Asp, Asn, His, Gln, Glu, and Lys at the membrane mid-plane cannot be determined precisely from the dsTβL assay.
source: We note that the energetic penalties for Asp, Asn, His, Gln, Glu, and Lys cannot be determined precisely from the dsTβL assay, since the number of reads for substitutions to these residues at the membrane mid-plane in the selected population is nearly 0
evidence: This is based on the low read counts in the deep-sequencing data.

claim: The hydrophobic residues, Val, Ile, Leu, Met, and Phe, show troughs at the membrane mid-plane.
source: At the membrane mid-plane, the hydrophobic residues, Val, Ile, Leu, Met, and Phe, show the expected troughs
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The trough for Val is shallower (approximately −0.5 kcal/mol) than for the large amino acids (<−1.5 kcal/mol).
source: which are shallower for the small amino acid Val (approximately −0.5 kcal/mol) than for the large amino acids (<−1.5 kcal/mol)
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: dsTβL fits well to the Moon scale (r2 = 0.90, with a slope close to 1).
source: dsTβL fits well to the Moon scale (Figure 2c, r2 = 0.90, with a slope close to 1), which similar to dsTβL measures substitution effects in a bacterial membrane – albeit the outer membrane (Moon and Fleming, 2011)
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison of dsTβL data with the Moon scale shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The correspondence between dsTβL and biophysical assays on purified proteins partly confirms the use of dsTβL for studying membrane-protein energetics.
source: The correspondence between dsTβL, which is based on in vivo measurement of membrane integration in a bacterial population, with biophysical assays on purified proteins, partly confirms the use of dsTβL for studying membrane-protein energetics.
evidence: This is inferred from the agreement between dsTβL and the Moon scale.

claim: The dsTβL profile for Trp is similar to the profiles of the aliphatic residues.
source: The dsTβL profile for Trp is similar to the profiles of the aliphatic residues
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Tyr makes a nearly neutral contribution to insertion in the membrane core.
source: whereas Tyr makes a nearly neutral contribution to insertion in the membrane core
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The dsTβL profiles for Tyr and Trp diverge from statistical inferences from membrane-protein structures and partitioning experiments.
source: These profiles diverge from statistical inferences from membrane-protein structures and partitioning experiments, which show that Tyr and Trp preferentially line the membrane-water interface (Ulmschneider et al., 2005; Schramm et al., 2012; Senes et al., 2007; Nakashima and Nishikawa, 1992; Yau et al., 1998)
evidence: This is based on comparison with multiple cited studies.

claim: In the dsTβL assay aromatic residues on the membrane-spanning segment lack neighboring aromatic residues with which to form stabilizing stacking interactions.
source: one possible explanation for these differences is that in the dsTβL assay aromatic residues on the membrane-spanning segment lack neighboring aromatic residues with which to form stabilizing stacking interactions
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed differences.

claim: Experimental stability measurements have shown that stacking makes a significant contribution to the net stabilization provided by aromatic residues in membrane proteins.
source: indeed, experimental stability measurements have shown that stacking makes a significant contribution to the net stabilization provided by aromatic residues in membrane proteins (Hong et al., 2007, 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental work.

claim: The apparent atomic-solvation parameter inferred from dsTβL is 37 ± 6 cal/mol/Å2.
source: We analyzed dsTβL data for 39 substitutions from one aliphatic residue (Ala, Val, Ile, Leu, and Met) to another at the core of the membrane (−9 Å<Z<13 Å) and inferred an apparent atomic-solvation parameter of 37 ± 6 cal/mol/Å2 (Figure 2d)
evidence: This is based on analysis of dsTβL data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The atomic-solvation parameter values inferred from dsTβL are in fair agreement with values for protein cores and hydrocarbons in aqueous solution.
source: The values we infer for the atomic-solvation parameter are therefore in fair agreement with values for protein cores and hydrocarbons in aqueous solution (Vajda et al., 1995)
evidence: This is based on comparison with cited values.

claim: The atomic-solvation parameter from dsTβL is 3–4 times larger than the value inferred from the Lep system.
source: and 3–4 times larger than the value inferred from the Lep system (Ojemalm et al., 2011)
evidence: This is based on comparison with the cited Lep system value.

claim: The ranking of apparent insertion free energies of aliphatic amino acids in dsTβL and Lep is similar (r2 = 0.79).
source: We further note that while the ranking of apparent insertion free energies of aliphatic amino acids in dsTβL and Lep (Hessa et al., 2007) is similar (r2 = 0.79, Figure 2—figure supplement 4)
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The magnitude of the insertion free-energy changes is nearly four times greater according to dsTβL compared to Lep.
source: the magnitude of the insertion free-energy changes is nearly four times greater according to dsTβL
evidence: This is based on comparison of dsTβL and Lep data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The hydrophobicity of the plasma membrane core is similar to that of hydrocarbons and much higher than measured in the Lep system.
source: We conclude that our results support the view that the hydrophobicity of the plasma membrane core is similar to that of hydrocarbons and much higher than measured in the Lep system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the atomic-solvation parameter analysis.

claim: The dsTβL profiles show clear and large asymmetries for Arg, Lys, and His, in agreement with the 'positive-inside' rule.
source: A striking feature of the dsTβL profiles, by contrast, is that they show clear and large asymmetries for Arg, Lys, and His, in agreement with the 'positive-inside' rule (Figure 2b)
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Lys and Arg are favored by 2 kcal/mol near the cytoplasm compared to near the periplasm.
source: whereas Lys and Arg are favored by 2 kcal/mol near the cytoplasm compared to near the periplasm
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: His shows a more modest asymmetry of 1 kcal/mol.
source: the titratable amino acid His shows a more modest asymmetry of 1 kcal/mol
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Only Arg stabilizes the segment near the cytosol, whereas Lys and His are nearly neutral at the cytosol-membrane interface.
source: moreover, of these three amino acids, only Arg stabilizes the segment near the cytosol, whereas Lys and His are nearly neutral at the cytosol-membrane interface
evidence: This is based on the insertion profiles shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The difference between Arg and Lys may be due to charge delocalization in the Arg sidechain and Arg's ability to form more hydrogen bonds with lipid phosphate headgroups.
source: This difference between Arg and Lys, which has not been noted until now, may be due to charge delocalization in the Arg sidechain and Arg's ability to form more hydrogen bonds with lipid phosphate headgroups.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed difference.

claim: Previous studies measured only a small energy difference (-0.5 kcal/mol) between inserting Arg and Lys in the cytoplasmic relative to the extracellular-facing side of the membrane.
source: but experimental quantification of the energetics of this asymmetry met with difficulty; previous studies measured only a small energy difference (-0.5 kcal/mol) between inserting Arg and Lys in the cytoplasmic relative to the extracellular-facing side of the membrane and no asymmetry for His (Lerch-Bader et al., 2008; Öjemalm et al., 2013)
evidence: This is based on cited previous studies.

claim: The insertion profiles could be used for bioinformatics prediction of the locations and orientations of membrane-spanning proteins.
source: Furthermore, the results suggest that the insertion profiles could be used for bioinformatics prediction of the locations and orientations of membrane-spanning proteins, [manuscript in preparation (Elazar et al.)]
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the observed propensities.

claim: The dsTβL profiles are similar to the knowledge-based ones for the weakly polar and hydrophobic residues (Val, Ser, and Thr).
source: The dsTβL profiles are similar to the knowledge-based ones for the weakly polar and hydrophobic residues (Val, Ser, and Thr)
evidence: This is based on comparison with knowledge-based profiles shown in Figure 4.

claim: The dsTβL profiles diverge from knowledge-based profiles with respect to the more hydrophobic and polar residues.
source: but they diverge with respect to the more hydrophobic and polar residues
evidence: This is based on comparison with knowledge-based profiles shown in Figure 4.

claim: The dsTβL apparent insertion energy for Leu, Ile, and Phe at the membrane mid-plane is −2 kcal/mol.
source: for instance, the dsTβL apparent insertion energy for Leu, Ile, and Phe at the membrane mid-plane is −2 kcal/mol and around −0.5kcal/mol for the other scales
evidence: This is based on the dsTβL data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The only knowledge-based scale that attempted to derive an asymmetric insertion potential reported much smaller asymmetries for Lys and Arg, of around 0.5 kcal/mol, compared to 2kcal/mol in dsTβL.
source: Additionally, the only knowledge-based scale that attempted to derive an asymmetric insertion potential (Schramm et al., 2012) reported much smaller asymmetries for Lys and Arg, of around 0.5 kcal/mol, compared to 2kcal/mol in dsTβL
evidence: This is based on comparison with the cited knowledge-based scale.

claim: Knowledge-based potentials reflect the frequencies of amino acids in membrane proteins and are biased by functional constraints.
source: These differences are likely due to the fact that knowledge-based potentials reflect the frequencies of amino acids in membrane proteins and are biased by functional constraints
evidence: This is an inference about the nature of knowledge-based potentials.

claim: Polar residues are often found in the membrane core, where they have important roles in oligomerization, substrate binding, transport, and conformational change.
source: indeed polar residues are often found in the membrane core, where they have important roles in oligomerization, substrate binding, transport, and conformational change
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about membrane protein function.

claim: Some of the amino acid positions that mediate self-association in GpA and ErbB2 according to their experimentally determined structures show large decreases in chloramphenicol viability upon mutation.
source: Some of the amino acid positions that mediate self-association in GpA and ErbB2 according to their experimentally determined structures (Bocharov et al., 2008; MacKenzie et al., 1997) show large decreases in chloramphenicol viability upon mutation
evidence: This is based on comparison of dsTβL data with known structures.

claim: Many mutations that have large effects on chloramphenicol viability are not close to the dimerization surfaces.
source: Unexpectedly, however, many other mutations that have large effects on chloramphenicol viability are not close to the dimerization surfaces (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on analysis of the mutational landscapes shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Factors other than self-association dominate the chloramphenicol-viability landscape.
source: suggesting that factors other than self-association dominate the chloramphenicol-viability landscape
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that many mutations affecting chloramphenicol viability are not at dimerization interfaces.

claim: The corrected self-association mutational landscapes correctly discriminate positions that mediate self-association from those that do not.
source: The corrected self-association mutational landscapes now correctly discriminate positions that mediate self-association from those that do not (Figure 5a)
evidence: This is based on the corrected mutational landscapes shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The corrected self-association mutational landscapes clearly highlight the interaction motifs in GpA and ErbB2.
source: and clearly highlight the interaction motifs in GpA and ErbB2
evidence: This is based on the corrected mutational landscapes shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The results from dsTβL and the previous TOXCAT study on GpA are consistent (r2 = 0.66).
source: The results from dsTβL and the previous study are consistent (r2 = 0.66; Figure 5b)
evidence: This is based on statistical comparison shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The consistency between dsTβL and the previous study confirms the use of the dsTβL insertion scale to correct self-association mutational landscapes in single-pass homodimers.
source: confirming the use of the dsTβL insertion scale to correct self-association mutational landscapes in single-pass homodimers
evidence: This is inferred from the agreement between dsTβL and previous TOXCAT results.

claim: GpA's Gly86 is sensitive to mutation but was previously not subjected to mutagenesis.
source: Furthermore, by systematically probing every position across the membrane, our results highlight additional positions that are sensitive to mutation, such as GpA's Gly86, which was previously not subjected to mutagenesis (Lemmon et al., 1992; Duong et al., 2007)
evidence: This is based on the dsTβL data and comparison with previous studies.

claim: Some mutations, for instance to Met in the GpA amino terminus, may promote self-association in the context of the TβL construct.
source: Moreover, it is notable that although the vast majority of mutations are either neutral or disruptive to self-association, some mutations, for instance to Met in the GpA amino terminus, may promote self-association in the context of the TβL construct (Figure 5a)
evidence: This is based on the corrected mutational landscapes shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The results confirm the strong interplay between membrane-protein expression levels and association.
source: Our results further confirm the strong interplay between membrane-protein expression levels and association
evidence: This is inferred from the need to correct for insertion effects in the self-association data.

claim: It is important to account for both insertion and association in biophysical experiments on membrane proteins.
source: and the importance of accounting for both in biophysical experiments on membrane proteins
evidence: This is inferred from the strong coupling observed between insertion and association.

claim: Fewer than five models passed the selection criteria for GpA and ErbB2 structure modeling.
source: In both cases, fewer than five models passed the selection criteria
evidence: This is based on the structure modeling results.

claim: Some models that passed the selection criteria were within 2 Å of experimentally determined structures.
source: and of those, some models were within 2 Å of experimentally determined structures
evidence: This is based on comparison of models with experimental structures.

claim: The systematic mutational landscapes generated by dsTβL can be used to provide constraints for structure modeling of receptor membrane domains.
source: We also tested whether the systematic mutational landscapes generated by dsTβL could be used to provide constraints for structure modeling of receptor membrane domains (Fleishman et al., 2002; Kim et al., 2003; Polyansky et al., 2014)
evidence: This is demonstrated by the structure modeling results shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The apparent insertion energies in dsTβL are in line with biophysical stability measurements on outer-membrane proteins.
source: The apparent insertion energies in dsTβL are in line with biophysical stability measurements on outer-membrane proteins (Moon and Fleming, 2011)
evidence: This is based on comparison with cited measurements.

claim: The inferred atomic-solvation parameter is close to measurements in model systems and protein cores.
source: and the inferred atomic-solvation parameter is close to measurements in model systems and protein cores (Andrew Karplus, 1997; Vajda et al., 1995)
evidence: This is based on comparison with cited measurements.

claim: The dsTβL measurements are three to four times larger than the corresponding ones using the Lep system.
source: Our measurements, however, are three to four times larger than the corresponding ones using the Lep system (Ojemalm et al., 2011; 2013; Hessa et al., 2007)
evidence: This is based on comparison with cited Lep system measurements.

claim: The observation that the dsTβL insertion measurements for aliphatic side chains have the same ranking but are fourfold larger in magnitude compared to those from Lep may indicate that the Lep system measures only a part of the energy contribution to insertion.
source: The observation that the dsTβL insertion measurements for aliphatic side chains have the same ranking but are fourfold larger in magnitude compared to those from Lep (Figure 2—figure supplement 4) may indicate that the Lep system measures only a part of the energy contribution to insertion
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed differences.

claim: The reason for the large differences between dsTβL and Lep may be that total membrane-protein expression levels were not quantified in the Lep system.
source: While further investigation is needed, we speculate that the reason for the large differences between dsTβL and Lep is that total membrane-protein expression levels were not quantified in the Lep system (Hessa et al., 2007; Ojemalm et al., 2011; 2013)
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed differences.

claim: The penalties for most polar residues at the membrane mid-plane are likely to indicate lower bounds on their insertion energies.
source: First, the penalties for most polar residues at the membrane mid-plane are likely to indicate lower bounds on their insertion energies, since the number of clones counted in the deep-sequencing data for these mutants is close to 0 (supplementary data)
evidence: This is inferred from the low read counts in the deep-sequencing data.

claim: Statistical analyses and experiments demonstrated that the aromatics Tyr and Trp are preferred in the water-membrane interface rather than in the core.
source: Second, statistical analyses (Ulmschneider et al., 2005; Schramm et al., 2012; Senes et al., 2007) and experiments (Hessa et al., 2007) demonstrated that the aromatics Tyr and Trp are preferred in the water-membrane interface rather than in the core, although dsTβL shows the reverse (Figure 2b)
evidence: This is based on cited statistical analyses and experiments.

claim: The dsTβL results for aromatics reflect the fact that dsTβL is based on a monomeric construct where the aromatics are fully exposed to the membrane environment.
source: We suggest that these results reflect the fact that dsTβL is based on a monomeric construct where the aromatics are fully exposed to the membrane environment
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed differences.

claim: The TOXCAT genetic screen has made essential contributions to our understanding of self-association in the membrane.
source: The TOXCAT genetic screen has made essential contributions to our understanding of self-association in the membrane (Lindner and Langosch, 2006; Lis and Blumenthal, 2006; Russ and Engelman, 1999; Finger et al., 2009; Mendrola et al., 2002; Li et al., 2004; Srinivasan et al., 2011﻿Reuven et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Some early reports demonstrated that chloramphenicol survival also depends on membrane-protein expression levels.
source: Some early reports demonstrated that chloramphenicol survival also depends on membrane-protein expression levels (Russ and Engelman, 1999; Duong et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Expression levels are a dominant factor in chloramphenicol survival.
source: Our results strongly support this view and show that expression levels are a dominant factor in chloramphenicol survival
evidence: This is inferred from the need to correct for insertion effects in the self-association data.

claim: A mutation's effects on monomer concentrations are counted twice in computing its effects on homodimer concentrations.
source: This dominance is perhaps not surprising in retrospect, given that a mutation's effects on monomer concentrations are counted twice in computing its effects on homodimer concentrations, and therefore on chloramphenicol viability (see equation (5) in Materials and methods)
evidence: This is based on the mathematical relationship between monomer and homodimer concentrations.

claim: A key contribution of unbiased and systematic assays, such as dsTβL, is that they clarify trends unambiguously.
source: A key contribution of unbiased and systematic assays, such as dsTβL, is that they clarify such trends unambiguously
evidence: This is a general statement about the value of systematic approaches.

claim: The dsTβL insertion profiles derived from the monomeric CLS provide a self-consistent way to factor out the contributions from insertion energetics in future assays on membrane-protein association or function in unrelated membrane proteins.
source: Furthermore, the dsTβL insertion profiles derived from the monomeric CLS provide a self-consistent way to factor out the contributions from insertion energetics in future assays on membrane-protein association or function in unrelated membrane proteins, thereby eschewing the need to measure the expression levels of individual mutants
evidence: This is a proposed application of the dsTβL insertion profiles.

claim: Deep mutational scanning has made important inroads to analysis and optimization of diverse protein systems.
source: Deep mutational scanning has made important inroads to analysis and optimization of diverse protein systems (Whitehead et al., 2012; Fowler and Fields, 2014; Boucher et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The main strengths of deep mutational scanning are the ability to measure the effects of all point mutations without bias and that all mutants experience strictly equal experimental conditions.
source: The main strengths of deep mutational scanning are the ability to measure the effects of all point mutations without bias and that all mutants experience strictly equal experimental conditions, thereby limiting experimental noise
evidence: This is a general statement about the advantages of deep mutational scanning.

claim: The structural simplicity of the model systems tested plays a role in the ability to accurately infer energetics.
source: The structural simplicity of the model systems tested here, consisting of a single α helix or of helix homodimers, plays a further role in the ability to accurately infer energetics
evidence: This is an inference about factors contributing to the success of the method.

claim: The data on protein-membrane and protein-protein energetics obtained from dsTβL will be used to improve models of membrane-protein energetics.
source: More generally the data on protein-membrane and protein-protein energetics obtained from dsTβL will be used to improve models of membrane-protein energetics and to design, screen, and engineer high-expression mutants of specific membrane proteins (Fleishman and Baker, 2012; Joh et al., 2014)
evidence: This is a proposed future application of the dsTβL data.

claim: Insertion of helix-forming segments into the membrane and their association determines the structure, function, and expression levels of all plasma membrane proteins.
source: Insertion of helix-forming segments into the membrane and their association determines the structure, function, and expression levels of all plasma membrane proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The hydrophobicity of biological membranes is significantly higher than appreciated.
source: revealing that the hydrophobicity of biological membranes is significantly higher than appreciated
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the dsTβL insertion data.

claim: There are large and unanticipated differences among positively charged residues in their contributions to membrane-protein insertion.
source: We further quantitate the contributions to membrane-protein insertion from positively charged residues at the cytoplasm-membrane interface and reveal large and unanticipated differences among these residues
evidence: This is based on the dsTβL insertion profiles for Arg, Lys, and His.

claim: Insertion and self-association are strongly coupled in receptor homodimers.
source: Finally, we derive comprehensive mutational landscapes in the membrane domains of Glycophorin A and the ErbB2 oncogene, and find that insertion and self-association are strongly coupled in receptor homodimers
evidence: This is based on the need to correct self-association data for insertion effects.

claim: Membrane-protein folding can be conceptually divided into two thermodynamic stages: the insertion into the membrane of transmembrane segments as α helices, and their association to form helix bundles.
source: Membrane-protein folding can be conceptually divided into two thermodynamic stages (Popot and Engelman, 1990; Cymer et al., 2015), each of which affects membrane-protein structure, function, and expression levels: the insertion into the membrane of transmembrane segments as α helices, and their association to form helix bundles (Ben-Tal et al., 1996; Heinrich and Rapoport, 2003; Moll and Thompson, 1994; White and Wimley, 1999; Popot and Engelman, 1990)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Important but fewer successes were reported in design of membrane proteins compared to soluble proteins, largely owing to the complexity of the plasma membrane and the lack of systematic and accurate measurements of membrane-protein energetics.
source: While significant progress has been made in structure prediction, design, and engineering of soluble proteins (Fleishman and Baker, 2012), important but fewer successes were reported in design of membrane proteins (Joh et al., 2014; Li et al., 2004), largely owing to the complexity of the plasma membrane and the lack of systematic and accurate measurements of membrane-protein energetics (Cymer et al., 2015)
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field, supported by citations.

claim: von Heijne and co-workers quantitated the partitioning of engineered peptides fused to the bacterial transmembrane protein, leader peptidase (Lep), between membrane-inserted and translocated states.
source: von Heijne and co-workers quantitated the partitioning of engineered peptides fused to the bacterial transmembrane protein, leader peptidase (Lep), between membrane-inserted and translocated states, and highlighted the importance of interactions between the translocon and the nascent polypeptide chain in determining partitioning (Hessa et al., 2007; Öjemalm et al., 2013)
evidence: This is based on cited previous work.

claim: The apparent atomic-solvation parameter according to the Lep measurements was only 10 cal/mol/Å2.
source: for instance, the apparent atomic-solvation parameter, which quantifies the free-energy contribution from the partitioning of hydrophobic surfaces to the membrane core, was only 10 cal/mol/Å2 according to the Lep measurements (Ojemalm et al., 2011)
evidence: This is based on cited previous work.

claim: Previous analyses reported an atomic-solvation parameter of ~30 cal/mol/Å2.
source: compared to ~30 cal/mol/Å2 from previous analyses (Andrew Karplus, 1997; Vajda et al., 1995)
evidence: This is based on cited previous work.

claim: The magnitude of the insertion free energies for individual amino acids were substantially lower according to the Lep system compared to other studies.
source: Additionally, the magnitude of the insertion free energies for individual amino acids were substantially lower according to the Lep system (Hessa et al., 2007; Ojemalm et al., 2011; Öjemalm et al., 2013) compared to other studies (Moon and Fleming, 2011; Shental-Bechor et al., 2006)
evidence: This is based on comparison of cited studies.

claim: These discrepancies led to suggestions that the Lep measurements were 'compressed' relative to others due to interactions between the engineered protein and other membrane constituents.
source: These discrepancies led to suggestions that the Lep measurements were 'compressed' relative to others due to interactions between the engineered protein and other membrane constituents (Johansson and Lindahl, 2009; Shental-Bechor et al., 2006)
evidence: This is based on cited previous work.

claim: Association is driven by packing interactions and short sequence motifs comprising small-xxx-small residues, where small is any of the small polar residues (Ser, Gly, or Ala) and x is any residue.
